title: Add delta/trend support to BigNumber

complexity.rationale: The rendering site (BigNumber.tsx) is precedented React presentational code, but the comparison-value semantics are an open design question (is the comparison a second dataKey, a literal prop, or derived from a prior row?), and formatting a signed percentage/absolute delta with directional styling is new, non-precedented logic not present anywhere else in BigNumber today.

summary: BigNumber currently supports an optional icon and/or sparkline (packages/react-spectrum-charts/src/rc/components/BigNumber/BigNumber.tsx) but has no way to show a delta/trend indicator (e.g. "+4.5%") next to the metric value. This request adds a new opt-in label option to render a computed change alongside the big number.
requirements: Add a new opt-in prop to BigNumberOptions/BigNumberProps that supplies a comparison value for the delta calculation (e.g. a second dataKey to diff against, or an explicit comparison value) — exact shape is an open design question, see openQuestions.

Compute the delta as a percentage (default) between the current bigNumberValue (from getBigNumberValue in BigNumber.tsx) and the comparison value; support absolute delta as an alternative if the design decision favors it.

Render the delta text near the formatted value (valueStyle text in BigNumberInternal), styled to indicate direction (e.g. positive/negative sign and color), using formatBigNumber-style locale-aware formatting from bigNumberFormatUtils.ts.
Delta rendering must work in both 'vertical' and 'horizontal' orientations and alongside the existing icon/sparkline layout without requiring a sparkline to be present.
Default behavior (prop omitted) must be unchanged — no delta rendered.

edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Percentage change is undefined (divide by zero); the component should show a defined fallback (e.g. omit the delta or show 'N/A') rather than NaN or Infinity.

edgeCases.case: Comparison dataKey/value is missing from the data
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Delta indicator is omitted entirely; the rest of BigNumber renders as it does today.

edgeCases.case: Delta shown together with icon and sparkline at 'small' bigNumberSize (chartWidth/height <= 100)
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Layout does not overflow or overlap; delta may need to be hidden or abbreviated at the smallest size, matching how label/value font sizes already scale via getFontSize.
Renders a neutral (non-colored, non-directional) state rather than defaulting to a positive or negative color.
Positive/negative delta colors must remain readable against both backgrounds, consistent with existing BigNumber.css conventions.

crossCutting.notes: BigNumber has no react-spectrum-charts-s2/vega-spec-builder-s2 component implementation today — only a type stub exists at packages/vega-spec-builder-s2/src/types/marks/bigNumberSpec.types.ts with no adapter or builder using it. There is nothing to keep in parity with in s2 yet.

implementationPlan.change: Add the new delta/trend field(s) to BigNumberOptions (optional, with JSDoc), following the existing pattern of numberFormat/numberType.
BigNumberProps extends BigNumberOptions via Omit — the new field passes through automatically unless it needs to be replaced with a ReactNode/callback.
In BigNumberInternal, compute the delta from data using a helper alongside getBigNumberValue, format it, and render it near the value text (valueStyle block).
Add a formatting helper for the signed delta (percentage or absolute), mirroring formatBigNumber's locale handling.
Add classes for positive/negative/neutral delta text color.
Document the new prop in the Props table with an example.
Add a story demonstrating the delta/trend indicator, positioned alongside existing icon/sparkline stories.

openQuestions: Should the comparison value be supplied as a second dataKey (diffed against the same aggregation method), an explicit numeric prop, or derived automatically (e.g. second-to-last vs last row)?
Should the delta always render as a percentage, or should it support an absolute-value mode, and if so via what prop?
Should directional styling use color alone, an arrow glyph, or both — and does this need a new Spectrum icon dependency?
